messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: kv-cache continuous-batching amplification detected in prod-west-2. Metric 'kv_evictions_per_sec' rose from ~4 to ~230 in 3m. Affected route: text.generate. Paging: @alex, @maria.

alex: ack — I'm on it, grabbing dashboards and tailing logs.

alex: initial look: spike aligns with scheduled job bulk-profiles-2026-03-15 (09:11 UTC) — seqlen distribution shows a heavy long-tail.

maria: checking traces now. continuous-batching queue depth -> large KV cache allocations per-shard. Tenant breakdown: bluewire ~78% of problematic requests. Prefetch + long seqs causing eviction storms.

chris: confirmed on traces. bluewire sent a burst of long prompts (avg ~9k tokens) which is growing KV entries and causing excessive paging. Latency/5xxs follow.

alex: impact numbers?

maria: region-wide error rate up to 2.8%, p95 latency +800ms. 4 customers seeing elevated 5xx; bluewire highest. Backpressure on continuous-batch path.

alex: mitigation plan (live):
1) Enable per-tenant batch override for bluewire (reduce batch_window_ms & max_microbatch).
2) Push a small canary global default lowering batch_window to reduce KV lifetime for new requests (10% traffic).
3) If unstable, enable emergency continuous-batch throttle (per-route) as a fallback.

chris: how quickly can we flip the per-tenant override?

sasha: use config-service API (internal). sample payload below.

sasha: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/flags/batch.window.override" 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{
    "target": "tenant:bluewire",
    "batch_window_ms": 8,
    "max_microbatch_size": 4,
    "note": "emergency mitigation for kv cache amplification"
  }'
```

alex: applying the per-tenant override now. will also create a canary config id cfg-20260315-01 and push to 5% hosts.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated — config push cfg-20260315-01 -> canary 5% hosts in prod-west-2. rollout id: cfg-20260315-01.

alex: flag set for tenant bluewire: batch_window_ms=8, max_microbatch_size=4. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/d/kv/kv-evictions?orgId=1&var-region=prod-west-2

maria: immediate signal: bluewire kv size per-shard down ~70% in 2 mins; evictions dropping; request errors decreasing.

chris: good. let's widen canary gradually. propose 5 -> 20% then 50 if stable for 10m.

alex: bumping canary to 20% now.

deploy-bot: canary widened to 20% (cfg-20260315-01). monitoring link: https://dash.internal/redwood/d/ops/rolling-deploys?uid=cfg-20260315-01

maria: stable for 12m at 20%: p95 trending back to baseline, evictions normalized. bluewire error volume back to baseline.

chris: recommend leaving per-tenant override for bluewire as permanent until we do a more holistic seqlen handling (pre-parse + watermarking). also roll global default to 20ms for all tenants to reduce KV lifetime.

alex: agreed. I'll open INC ticket and schedule postmortem. created INC-9876.

sre_lead: add action items:
- postmortem with timeline and root cause (seqlen ingestion job)
- add seqlen-based alert (if median seqlen > X or 99th > Y) to catch bulk imports
- add automatic per-tenant throttle if KV growth rate > threshold
- bake runbook steps for per-tenant override and canary expansion

oncall-bot: Incident logged (INC-9876). Paging cleared.

maria: I've updated runbook draft and threshold suggestions in the incident doc. tagging @sre_lead for review. :thumbsup: 

alex: thanks all. I'll follow up with a short summary and remediation PR for config-service to expose a safer quick-toggle for per-tenant batch overrides. moving to monitoring state; will close thread once PR + runbook merged.

sasha: note — recommend adding rate-limit on config-service flag flips (audit) to avoid accidental rapid toggles.

chris: one last note — add durable guard in serving runtime: if kv cache size delta > 5x in 1m for a tenant, treat as safety and fall back to per-request small-batch mode automatically.

alex: capturing all items in INC-9876. Good work everyone.

oncall-bot: This thread will auto-close in 24h if no new messages.
